name: atasm
desc: Atari MAC/65 compatible assembler for Unix
why: An assembler for the Atari 8-bit MAC/65 dialect, an old-school environment that opens a door into retro machine code.

brief.what_it_is: ATasm is a command-line cross-assembler for the 6502 CPU, written in C. It reads 6502 assembly source and produces Atari 8-bit binary load files. It can also write .XFD or .ATR disk images, or Atari800 and Atari++ machine state files. The README says it is mostly compatible with the Mac/65 macro assembler from OSS Software, so existing Mac/65 source and macro libraries should assemble with it.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the aim is to let Atari home-brew coders edit and build with modern editors instead of the original Mac/65 cartridge editor, which one reviewer called excruciating. It says code can be built quickly on a modern machine.
brief.install_notes: Download atasm109.zip from the SourceForge Files page (397.7 kB). The package includes all source code and a Windows binary. The README says it compiles cleanly on Linux, macOS/X, or any platform with GNU C or Clang, so on Unix you build from source. The README gives no build command, and I saw no runtime, account, or configuration steps. The Homebrew formula name is atasm.
brief.standout: It is a drop-in path for old Mac/65 code: the project's own README describes it as compatible with an existing macro assembler, and it targets Atari disk images and emulator state files directly. The Atari-specific directives and undocumented opcode support also set it apart from a generic 6502 assembler.
brief.status: Quiet. The SourceForge page and README both show last update 2021-03-21, with a README copyright notice of 1998-2021 and a 2021 modification by Peter Hinz. The project was registered 2002-06-15. It has 7 downloads per week and 2 user reviews, from 2012 and 2013. I found no later release or commit.
brief.caveats: The README says 'mostly' Mac/65 compatible, so some Mac/65 code may need changes. Licence is GPLv2. The Windows binary is included, but on Unix you have to compile it yourself. The README gives no build instructions or usage examples, and I did not find a separate docs site. The SourceForge page lists the project as 'Brought to you by' a single maintainer, schmelze.
quotes: ATasm is a 6502 command-line cross-assembler that is compatible with the original Mac/65 macroassembler released by OSS software.
Code development can now be performed using "modern" editors and compiles with lightning speed.
ATasm runs native on IBM PCs in Windows and compiles cleanly under Linux, MacOS/X or any platform with the GNU C or Clang compiler.
fetch_log: https://sourceforge.net/projects/atasm/ : worked, but the page is mostly site chrome; it gave the description, feature list, GPLv2 licence, last update 2021-03-21, and the reviews. No README text or commands were shown.
https://sourceforge.net/projects/atasm/files/ : worked; contained the README.md text (ATasm v1.09) and the atasm109.zip download entry. No command lines appear in it.
